chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a grave whose inhabitant was being punished. Then he passed by it the following year, and behold, he was not being punished. So he said: 'O Lord! I passed by this grave the first year, so he was being punished, and I passed by it this year and he is not being punished.' So Allah revealed to him: 'A righteous son of his has come of age, so he repaired a road and sheltered an orphan, thus for this I have forgiven him for what his son did.'
Then Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The inheritance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His believing servant is a son who worships Him after him.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Verse of Zakariyya (peace be upon him): 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a successor. Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqoub, and make him, my Lord, one with whom You are well pleased.'
ai.seo_question: How can the righteous deeds of a son lead to the forgiveness of his father in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia doctrine of 'Husn al-Khatimah' (good ending) facilitated by the enduring merit of offspring, where a son’s specific acts of charity—such as improving a path or sheltering an orphan—can expiate the father's sins. By linking this to the supplication of Prophet Zakariyya, the Imam emphasizes that a righteous heir serves as a spiritual continuation of the believer's legacy, effectively acting as Allah's 'inheritance' from the deceased. This underscores the practical Islamic principle that familial piety extends beyond biological lineage to encompass moral and spiritual stewardship.
